text: Seabrook Town secures a 4-2 victory over Harbour City after trailing 2-0 early in the second half [#905] [#975] [#1104]. Harbour City opens scoring at the left side of Seabrook’s penalty area, with Elias Okafor finishing a 17-pass buildup from their midfield [#904] [#905]. Marek Barros then scores from the right corner after a quick cross [#973] [#975]. Seabrook responds swiftly with Tariq Marlowe winning the ball near midfield and scoring from 10 metres out at the centre of Harbour City’s half [#1103] [#1104]. After increasing their pressing and playing more direct from the 65th minute, Seabrook takes advantage of turnovers high up the pitch, with Callum Varga scoring inside Harbour City’s box on the left flank [#1361] [#1448]. Near the end, Kian Romano nets two quick goals: first from close range on the right side after a fast counterattack, then again from a short pass inside the penalty area to turn the match [#1882] [#1906]. Harbour City had to play nearly half the game with 10 men after a red card, an important factor in Seabrook’s comeback [#871].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with a significantly higher xG of 3.53 compared to Harbour City's 1.26, leading to a 4-2 victory [#1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros was key for Harbour City with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, and 9 interceptions, earning a rating of 10.0 [#975].
- Harbour City had fewer shots (10) and shots on target (5) than Seabrook Town (22 shots, 9 on target), indicating less offensive threat [team_stats].
- Harbour City played with 10 men after Joon Whitfield was red-carded at 43', which likely affected their defensive and offensive capabilities [#871].
- Seabrook Town increased pressing and directness after 65', which helped them turn the game around with 4 second-half goals [#1361].

- Harbour City’s opening goal at 45’ came after a long, patient build-up involving 17 passes over 57 seconds, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style. Elias Okafor's goal was assisted by Marek Barros via a through pass, indicating effective buildup rather than direct attack [904,905]. This shows Harbour trying to break down Seabrook’s 3-4-3 defensive shape with methodical possession.

- Marek Barros' second goal at 47’ originated from a corner situation, capitalizing on a quick cross after just one pass in 28 seconds. This suggests Harbour used set pieces to create overloads in attacking areas, contrasting their usual patient style, possibly exploiting Seabrook’s 3-4-3 defensive vulnerabilities on set pieces [973,975].

- Seabrook Town’s first goal at 53’ came from a regain (ball recovery) by Tariq Marlowe and was scored quickly (within 1 second, no passes involved), demonstrating a fast counter-attacking threat characteristic of their more direct, wide crossing play within the 3-4-3 setup. Marlowe's action highlighted how Seabrook exploited turnovers to transition quickly [1103,1104].

- Following tactical changes at 65’, where Seabrook pushed higher press intensity, played more direct, and raised their defensive line (line height from 0.6 to 0.72), they scored twice more (69’, 90+2’) through a combination of regained possession and quick, direct attacks. Callum Varga's goal at 69’ involved a short passing sequence from a regain, emphasizing pressing to force turnovers and rapid attack [1361,1447,1448]. Kian Romano’s equalizing and winning goals near the end came from quick counter and short passing sequences, confirming Seabrook’s effective adaptation to a higher press and direct style late in the game [1881,1882,1905,1906].
